blocks.prompt: 4. A particle moving along a coordinate line at time \(t = 0\) is at a position 2 cm from the origin and traveling at a velocity of 5 cm/sec. If the acceleration of the particle is given by \(a(t) = 3 - 4(t + 2)^{-3}\), find the velocity and the position of the particle as functions of \(t\).
blocks.explanation:
Two integrations: acceleration \(\to\) velocity \(\to\) position, each with its own constant.
Given: \(s(0) = 2\), \(v(0) = 5\), \(a(t) = 3 - 4(t+2)^{-3}\).
Plan: integrate \(a\) (power rule on \((t+2)^{-3}\)), use \(v(0) = 5\); integrate \(v\), use \(s(0) = 2\).
steps:
Given: \(a(t) = 3 - 4(t + 2)^{-3}\), \(v(0) = 5\) cm/s, \(s(0) = 2\) cm.
To find: \(v(t)\) and \(s(t)\).
Method: \(v = \int a\,dt\), \(s = \int v\,dt\); the two starting values fix the two constants.

Integrate the acceleration
\[v(t) = \int\big(3 - 4(t + 2)^{-3}\big)\,dt\]
\[= 3t - 4\cdot\dfrac{(t + 2)^{-2}}{-2} + c_1\]
\[= 3t + \dfrac{2}{(t + 2)^{2}} + c_1\]
Why: \(\int (t + 2)^{n}\,dt = \frac{(t + 2)^{n+1}}{n + 1}\) with \(n = -3\) (the inside \(t + 2\) has derivative 1).

Integrate the velocity
\[s(t) = \int\left(3t + 2(t + 2)^{-2} + \dfrac{9}{2}\right)dt\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{2}t^{2} + 2\cdot\dfrac{(t + 2)^{-1}}{-1} + \dfrac{9}{2}t + c_2\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{2}t^{2} - \dfrac{2}{t + 2} + \dfrac{9}{2}t + c_2\]
Why: power rule again with \(n = -2\).
